definitions.meaning: the length of the third month of the year
a piece written for soldiers to step in time to

explanation.surface: A month-long festival of brass-band music for the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: The month after February has thirty-one days, and a quick-step tune for troops on parade is also called by this word.

clue.text: Way in which lawn was cut, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for the cut lawn is spoken, and a word sounding the same is wanted

parts.note: grass that has been cut has been mowed

explanation.surface: Someone explaining the manner in which the gardener trimmed the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a manner or method of doing something, a synonym of way.

clue.text: Tall grass in which animals turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word is written from the bottom upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: deer are animals; the word serves as its own plural

explanation.surface: Wildlife appearing among long grasses in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are tall grass-like plants growing in wet ground, a fair loose synonym.

clue.text: Farm work provides married man with endless cereal

parts.note: a married man is a husband

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the cereal word is cut off

parts.note: rye is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A farmer's wife says the husband supplies the grain for the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbandry is the old word for agriculture, the care of crops and animals on a farm.

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters of Monday's sit clumsily and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that the start of the week is a bad day for the people who supply things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'present-day' but means electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamos are generators that supply electric current.

clue.text: Obtain parking place outside house finally

indicators.note: outside says the parking word goes round the other letter

parts.note: a drive is the private road in front of a house where a car is parked

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of house

explanation.surface: Instructions to get a parking space in front of a house at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E, the last letter of 'house', which goes inside DRIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To derive something is to get or obtain it from a source.

clue.text: Requirement for tennis? Put up half of it

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means written from the bottom upwards, so read backwards
half of keeps the first three of its six letters

parts.note: it points back to the tennis just mentioned

explanation.surface: Setting up a tennis court: the net is needed, so put up half of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes TEN from TENNIS, and 'Put up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis match cannot be played without the mesh barrier across the middle of the court.

indicators.note: found in says the numeral sits inside the church word

parts.note: a minster is a large church, like York Minster
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A priest being located inside a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a member of the clergy, especially in Protestant churches.

indicators.note: in a down entry, rise means the word is written going upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: in Britain puddings are desserts, the sweet course

explanation.surface: A tense baker watching puddings rise in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puddings' is the British word for the sweet course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stressed is strained and anxious, as if under pressure.

definitions.meaning: a theatre assistant who helps actors into costume, or anyone getting clothed
a kitchen cabinet with shelves for crockery

explanation.surface: Someone laying garments on top of a sideboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre helper who clothes actors and a piece of kitchen furniture with shelves share this name.

clue.text: Singer taking part in Britten oratorio

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A vocalist performing in a choral work by the composer Benjamin Britten.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with a high voice, a kind of singer.

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort the letters again into a new order

explanation.surface: Churchgoers taking a trip to a seaside town in Lancashire, an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a seaside town but is read as 're-sort', the anagram signal. Lancs is short for Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvinists are Protestants following the teaching of John Calvin, so religious people.

indicators.note: in says the river and rodent letters go inside the word for unsophisticated

parts.note: naive means innocent and unsophisticated
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A simple tale about a water rat, like The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of events, a story.

indicators.note: changed says the letters of Colin has are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Colin has adopted a new name.
explanation.walkthrough: Colin is itself a short form of the name made by the anagram, which adds charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas is a man's given name, so a fair answer to 'his name'.

parts.note: to defame someone is to slander them

explanation.surface: A speaker confessing to slandering someone from Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey is one of the Channel Islands, off the coast of France.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jerseyman lives on an island, so he is an example of an island dweller.

parts.note: something fashionable is in
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A stylish football team serving a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside is slang for being in prison, which is what doing time means.

clue.text: Air gently moving piece of cake

explanation.surface: A slice of cake being wafted through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A light wind is one sense; a task done with no effort is the slang sense, both meaning ease.

clue.text: Hard ground that's by the fire

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the noun, the place at the fire

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
the ground is earth

explanation.surface: A solid patch of floor beside a fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: The hearth is the stone floor in front of and around a fireplace.

clue.text: Lead, for example, in a type of rock

definitions.meaning: lead is a dense, weighty metallic element
a loud style of guitar music

explanation.surface: A geologist describing lead ore found within a kind of stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' sounds geological but means rock music.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a dense metal, and a loud guitar-based genre of rock music shares the same two-word name.

clue.text: People start to understand list of options

parts.note: men are people

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of understand

explanation.surface: People beginning to grasp what choices they have.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is a list of dishes in a restaurant, or of choices on a computer screen.

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: Ranking pubs: this one is the runner-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but is the verb meaning prevent.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar something is to block or prevent it, so a synonym for stop.

parts.note: le is French for the
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A French teacher is lured into something.
explanation.definitionFit: To be led on is to be lured or tempted along, the same as being enticed.

clue.text: Silly-billy in kilt with odd bits missing

indicators.note: dropping the first, third and fifth letters keeps only the even ones

explanation.surface: A fool in a kilt with some odd parts missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' belongs to the letter run, not a link word: from I-N-K-I-L-T only the even letters stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A nit, short for nitwit, is a foolish person.

indicators.note: in says the goal word sits inside the torn word

parts.note: rent is an old word meaning torn
an aim is an object or goal

explanation.surface: An item lying among ripped clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' is the noun meaning purpose, not a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old or literary word for clothes.

clue.text: Mark is to withdraw from contest

definitions.meaning: a shallow line or graze on a surface
to pull out of a race or competition

explanation.surface: A competitor named Mark is pulling out of a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A light graze on a surface and pulling out of a race share this word.

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark

explanation.surface: Providing someone from Europe with a witty line.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish someone with things is to supply or equip them.
